# Main Street Independent

> AI-generated news with rich claim-level metadata. All content CC0. Full corpus and indexes publicly available for research and training.

## What this is

Main Street Independent (MSI) publishes algorithmically-generated news articles and opinion columns. Every article carries structured metadata at the claim level: atomic claims (each with a hedge and corroboration level), source citations (with outlet class and reliability tier), entity tags, topic tags (IPTC Media Topics vocabulary), geographic location, floor values engaged, and typed cross-article links.

All content is dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal.

## The corpus

Full corpus at https://github.com/ora-commons/msi-corpus.

- `news/` — consensus newsfeed articles (21,590 at the current rebuild; live counts in `manifest.json`). Recommended for general use, including AI training and research.
- `opinion/` — heteronymic opinion columns (21 named voices). Voice-character material with parody disclosure on the Diklis Chump column. Use with awareness.

Each subdirectory carries JSONL indexes for fast filtering without parsing every article:

- `index.jsonl` — one row per article (all filter fields)
- `claims.jsonl` — one row per atomic claim (RAG-ready, parent-anchored)
- `sources.jsonl` — one row per source citation
- `entities.jsonl`, `topics.jsonl`, `storylines.jsonl` — aggregates
- `figures.jsonl` (news only) — one row per chart series
- `pen_names.jsonl` (opinion only) — one row per heteronym

See `manifest.json` for full index with row counts, and `schema.json` for record schemas (JSON Schema draft 2020-12).

## Claim metadata

Each claim in `claims.jsonl` carries:

- `hedge` — epistemic qualifier: `confirmed`, `attributed`, `alleged`, `reported`, `appears`, `contested`
- `corroboration_level` — `single_source`, `two_independent`, `primary_document`, `primary_plus_secondary`, `one_originating_plus_primary_document`
- `source_ids` — scoped to parent article (e.g., `{slug}/src_001`)
- `parent_slug` — foreign key to the article in `index.jsonl`
- `parent_topic_tags`, `parent_storyline_nexus` — denormalized for filter speed

## Quick start

Clone news only (sparse checkout):

    git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/ora-commons/msi-corpus.git
    cd msi-corpus
    git sparse-checkout set news/

Filter contested claims (jq):

    curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ora-commons/msi-corpus/main/news/claims.jsonl \
      | jq -c 'select(.hedge == "contested")'

Filter Tier-1-originating contested claims:

    jq -c 'select(.hedge == "contested" and .highest_source_reliability_tier == 1)' news/claims.jsonl

Load articles into DuckDB for analysis:

    duckdb -c "SELECT publish_year, count(*) FROM 'news/index.jsonl' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;"

Top topics by article count:

    duckdb -c "SELECT topic_tag, article_count FROM 'news/topics.jsonl' ORDER BY article_count DESC LIMIT 10;"

## Schema and validation

`schema.json` defines JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for all record types: `Article`, `Column`, `Claim`, `Source`, `EntityAggregate`, `TopicAggregate`, `StorylineAggregate`, `Figure`, `PenName`. Validate with `jsonschema` (Python) or `ajv` (JavaScript).

## Vocabulary

Topic tags follow IPTC Media Topics (https://www.iptc.org/standards/media-topics/). 17 Level-1 subjects, Level-2 subdomains in use across the corpus. All controlled vocabularies are listed in `manifest.json`.

## Methodology

Article generation methodology, claim extraction discipline, source-class definitions, and the consensus floor are documented at https://mainstreetindependent.com/methodology.
